content: 1. Information regarding the quantitative effects of CYP3A4 inducers on amlodipine is available. Blood pressure should be closely monitored when amlodipine is co-administered with CYP3A4 inducers. 2. Levoketoconazole increases the levels or effects of etravirine by influencing hepatic enzyme CYP2C9/10 metabolism. Close monitoring is required. 3. Ketoconazole, a CYP3A4 inhibitor and substrate, may increase plasma concentrations of etravirine, while etravirine may decrease ketoconazole plasma concentrations. Use caution and monitor closely. 4. Etravirine decreases the levels or effects of levonorgestrel (intrauterine or oral) by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Hormonal contraceptive efficacy may be reduced; alternative or backup contraception is recommended when enzyme inducers are used with combined hormonal contraceptives (CHCs). Backup contraception should continue for 28 days after discontinuing the enzyme inducer. 5. Etravirine decreases the levels or effects of linagliptin by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 6. Etravirine decreases the levels or effects of lomitapide by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 7. Etravirine decreases the levels or effects of lonafarnib by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration with strong or moderate CYP3A4 inducers is contraindicated as lonafarnib is a sensitive CYP3A4 substrate. 8. Etravirine decreases the levels or effects of lopinavir by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism, while lopinavir increases the levels or effects of etravirine. Use caution and monitor closely. 9. Etravirine decreases the levels or effects of loratadine by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 10. Etravirine decreases the levels or effects of lorlatinib by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration with strong CYP3A4 inducers is contraindicated. 11. Etravirine decreases the levels or effects of losartan by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism, but it may also increase losartan levels via CYP2C9/10 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 12. Etravirine decreases the levels or effects of lovastatin by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 13. Etravirine may interfere with the manufacturing of lovotibeglogene autotemcel. Antiretroviral therapy (ART) should be discontinued at least one month before mobilization and until all apheresis cycles are completed. Some long-acting ARTs may require a longer discontinuation period. 14. Etravirine decreases the levels or effects of lumacaftor/ivacaftor by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration with strong CYP3A4 inducers can reduce ivacaftor exposure by 57%, potentially reducing efficacy. Monitor closely. 15. Etravirine decreases the levels or effects of lurasidone by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Dose adjustments may be necessary after chronic treatment with moderate CYP3A inducers. 16. Etravirine decreases the levels or effects of lurbinectedin by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 17. Etravirine decreases the levels or effects of macimorelin by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration with strong CYP3A4 inducers may lead to false-positive test results. Discontinue the inducer and allow for sufficient washout time before testing. 18. Etravirine decreases the levels or effects of macitentan by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration with strong CYP3A4 inducers. 19. Etravirine decreases the levels or effects of maraviroc by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 20. Marijuana increases the levels or effects of etravirine by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 21. Etravirine increases or decreases the levels or effects of mavacamten by affecting hepatic enzyme CYP2C19 and CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration is contraindicated. 22. Etravirine increases the levels or effects of mavorixafor by P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Monitor closely and adjust the dose if needed. 23. Etravirine decreases the levels or effects of medroxyprogesterone by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Contraceptive failure is possible; use an alternative if available. 24. Etravirine decreases the levels or effects of mefloquine by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 25. Etravirine increases the levels or effects of meloxicam by affecting hepatic enzyme CYP2C9/10 metabolism. The clinical significance is unknown; monitor closely. 26. Etravirine decreases the levels or effects of mestranol by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 27. Etravirine decreases the levels or effects of methadone by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 28. Etravirine decreases the levels or effects of methylprednisolone by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 29. Metronidazole increases the levels or effects of etravirine by affecting hepatic enzyme CYP2C9/10 and CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 30. Miconazole vaginal increases the levels or effects of etravirine by affecting hepatic enzyme CYP2C9/10 and CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 31. Etravirine decreases the levels or effects of midazolam by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 32. Etravirine decreases the levels or effects of midostaurin by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration with strong CYP3A4 inducers may reduce midostaurin concentrations and efficacy. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 33. Etravirine decreases the levels or effects of mifepristone by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration is not recommended by the manufacturer. 34. Etravirine decreases the levels or effects of mirtazapine by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 35. Mitotane decreases the levels of etravirine by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Mitotane is a strong CYP3A4 inducer; monitor for potential dosage adjustments. 36. Modafinil increases the levels or effects of etravirine by affecting hepatic enzyme CYP2C19 metabolism, while etravirine decreases the levels or effects of modafinil by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 37. Etravirine decreases the levels or effects of montelukast by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance is unknown; monitor closely. 38. Nafcillin decreases the levels or effects of etravirine by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 39. Etravirine decreases the levels or effects of naldemedine by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Simulation studies suggest moderate CYP3A4 inducers decrease naldemedine exposure. Monitor for adverse effects. 40. Etravirine decreases the levels or effects of naloxegol by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration with strong CYP3A4 inducers is not recommended. 41. Etravirine increases the levels or effects of nateglinide by affecting hepatic enzyme CYP2C9/10 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 42. Etravirine decreases the levels or effects of nefazodone by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 43. Etravirine increases the levels of nelfinavir by decreasing its metabolism. Monitor closely for potential interactions. 44. Etravirine decreases the levels or effects of neratinib by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration with strong/moderate CYP3A4 inducers. 45. Etravirine decreases the levels or effects of netupitant/palonosetron by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 46. Nevirapine decreases the levels of etravirine by increasing its metabolism. Co-administration is contraindicated. 47. Etravirine decreases the levels or effects of nicardipine by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 48. Etravirine decreases the levels or effects of nifedipine by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Modify therapy and monitor closely. 49. Etravirine increases the levels of nintedanib by P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Monitor closely for adverse effects. 50. Etravirine decreases the levels or effects of nirogacestat by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 51. Etravirine decreases the levels or effects of nisoldipine by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 52. Nitisinone increases the levels or effects of etravirine by inhibiting CYP2C9. Caution is advised when co-administering CYP2C9 substrates, especially those with a narrow therapeutic index.
